status: PROPOSED_UNVERIFIED_TO_PASS — real backtest run, HONEST FAIL
name: Tactical Rotation + Strategic Risk-Parity + Cash Floor
fusion_methodology: Equal-weight (flat 1/3 each — NOT tuned, the least-discretionary choice available) blend of each leg's own daily return series, date-aligned by inner join on daily_return_dates, combined as a DAILY rebalance to fixed weights: r_fused[t] = (r_antonacci[t] + r_maillard[t] + r_tbill[t]) / 3. This is a modeling simplification (a real product would more likely rebalance monthly/quarterly, not daily) — flagged, not hidden.

data.source: real, non-synthetic — yfinance OHLCV, 2004-01-02..2026-04-30 fetch window
data.date_range_note: Limited to 2007-05-30 onward by BIL's real inception date (BIL launched 2007-05-25) — NOT the antonacci/maillard legs' own longer 2004-2026 native window. A leg-only stat computed on its native longer window (as in the doc's priors) is not apples-to-apples with this fused number.
data.known_caveat_capital_preservation_tbill: capital_preservation_tbill's live/legacy DB fixture (sharpe=0.481, cagr=2.91%) was NOT reproduced by a literal run_backtest(BIL) — BIL's raw (non-dividend-adjusted) Close is flat (+0.04% total return over 19 years) because virtually all of a T-bill ETF's return is distributions, not price appreciation. This script uses dividend-adjusted BIL (auto_adjust=True) instead, which correctly captures +28.7% total / ~1.3%/yr CAGR over the same window. See docs/CURATED-CONSOLIDATION-BUILD-2026-07-09.md for the full diagnosis. Flagging for Dan/Önder: the standard fetch_ohlcv pipeline (auto_adjust=False) would silently mis-backtest capital_preservation_tbill if it were ever added to regen_fixtures.py as-is.

verified_real_verdict.verdict: HONEST FAIL. Does not clear the rigor gate at any strictness level (1-5).

what_worked: PBO = 0.108 (well under the 0.50 ceiling) — the combination is NOT overfit / curve-fit by the CSCV test.
OOS Sharpe (+0.439) is positive and exceeds the in-sample Sharpe (-0.111) — no in-sample-to-out-of-sample performance cliff.
Look-ahead audit passes (real backtrader run, no cheat-on-close/open).
corrections_2026_07_13_pr1078_review: RETRACTED: 'correlation_to_spy = -0.009, near-zero, genuinely uncorrelated'. Date-aligned, the fused candidate's SPY correlation is +0.210 — a real but materially weaker diversification benefit than originally claimed. The -0.009 was a calendar-misalignment artifact (12.4% of pairs matched to wrong days).

CORRECTED: the 2-leg (no cash floor) comparison row was computed on the blend's native 2004-2026 window (n=5268), not the stated common 2007-2026 window (n=4467). Corrected apples-to-apples DSR p = 0.0754 (was misreported as 0.0943; that figure belongs to the incomparable native window). The qualitative finding — dropping the cash floor improves deflated significance — survives.
Per-leg date-aligned SPY correlations (native windows): antonacci +0.096 (genuinely low), maillard +0.360 (NOT low/negative — the legacy -0.019 was the same misalignment artifact), tbill -0.119.
what_failed: DSR p-value (0.0245) is far below both the 0.90 badge bar and the 0.50 always-on floor — the deflated, multiple-testing-corrected significance of the fused Sharpe is very weak.

Root cause (diagnosed, not fixed by reweighting): the fused Sharpe at rf=5%/yr is only +0.072 — barely above zero — because the cash-floor leg's OWN Sharpe under the codebase's flat 5%/yr risk-free convention is deeply negative (-7.3) in this specific window: actual T-bill yields were near 0% for large stretches of 2007-2015 and 2020-2021 (two ZIRP eras), so ANY genuinely-risk-free instrument looks catastrophic against a flat 5%/yr hurdle in this exact sample. This is a convention artifact, not a strategy defect — but it materially drags down the fused Sharpe, and DSR is very sensitive to a Sharpe this close to zero.

antonacci_plus_maillard_NATIVE_2004_2026.note: The blend's own native window, ~3.2y longer incl. pre-GFC — NOT comparable to the rows above; kept for context because the original (buggy) same-window row actually reported these values.

supplementary_comparison_same_window_num.note: All rows except the explicitly-labeled native-window context row are computed on the SAME 2007-2026 common window (n=4467) and num_trials=34 as the 3-leg fused candidate, for a true apples-to-apples comparison. (The original version of this block misreported the 2-leg row: it was computed on the native window — window-mismatch bug caught in PR #1078 review, corrected 2026-07-13.) Corrected finding: dropping the cash-floor leg (2-leg 50/50 Antonacci+Maillard) scores BETTER on DSR (p=0.0754) than the 3-leg blend (p=0.0245) — the cash floor's near-zero-yield-vs-5%-hurdle problem in this window HURTS the deflated significance more than the extra diversification helps it. This is reported as a finding, not acted on by re-weighting (that would be tuning to pass).

recommendation: Do NOT promote to the live library as-is. Two honest, non-tuning paths forward for Dan/Önder to consider: (1) re-evaluate the cash-floor leg's fair treatment given the flat 5%/yr rf convention was not designed with a genuinely risk-free instrument in mind — this is a modeling-convention question, not a strategy question; (2) the 2-leg Antonacci+Maillard (no cash floor) variant scores better on deflated significance (corrected same-window DSR p=0.0754 vs 0.90 needed — still far from passing) and may be worth a from-scratch, non-tuned re-verification as its own candidate in a future pass. Neither path is executed here — both would need Dan/Önder sign-off before any further real-data run is used to justify a claim.
